retainedFindings.title: `partition()` drops all jobs beyond the first batch
retainedFindings.body: Trigger: any `reviewBatch(jobs, {limit})` call where `jobs.length > limit`. `partition()` now returns `[jobs.slice(0, limit)]` instead of chunking the full array, so jobs after `limit` are silently dropped and never returned in any batch. This breaks the retained contract in AGENTS.md that all submitted jobs must appear in the returned batches exactly once and that the limit is a per-batch capacity, not a limit on total jobs processed. Consider restoring the loop `for (let i = 0; i < jobs.length; i += limit) batches.push(jobs.slice(i, i + limit))`.

This breaks the unchanged caller which expects full coverage via `.flat()`, and violates the retained `AGENTS.md` contract that all submitted jobs must appear in the returned batches exactly once with `limit` as per-batch capacity. Consider restoring the loop that slices all batches.

retainedFindings.title: `partition()` drops all jobs after the first batch
retainedFindings.body: Trigger: call `drain()` in `src/worker.ts:2` with more than 100 jobs, e.g. 250 jobs with `{ limit: 100 }`. `reviewBatch()` now calls `partition()` which returns `[jobs.slice(0, limit)]`, so `.flat()` yields only the first 100 jobs and silently drops the remaining 150. This is wrong because the prior `partition()` looped `i += limit` to cover every job, and `AGENTS.md` requires all submitted jobs appear in returned batches exactly once with the limit as per-batch capacity, not a total cap. Consider restoring the loop: `for (let i = 0; i < jobs.length; i += limit) batches.push(jobs.slice(i, i + limit))`.
